claims.text: The investigated HEA is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr consists of refractory elements.
The WTaTiVZr HEA has a random elemental distribution and severe lattice distortion.
At high temperature, equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain and toughness than commercially used pure tungsten.
Random solid-solution lattice distortion is the primary cause of the HEA's enhanced plastic strain and toughness.
Severe lattice distortion lowers the local Peierls barrier in WTaTiVZr.
Lowering the Peierls barrier activates a broader range of dislocation glide systems.
Lattice distortion increases dislocation nucleation in the HEA relative to pure tungsten.
Lattice distortion increases dislocation mobility in the HEA relative to pure tungsten.
Severe lattice distortion and compositional fluctuations alter dislocation-line configurations in BCC HEAs.
The proposed comparison uses approximately 1200°C uniaxial tensile loading with comparable strain rates, geometries, and environments for the HEA and tungsten.
In situ TEM coupled with DIC can quantitatively monitor dislocation generation, glide velocity, nucleation frequency, and strain evolution under the proposed conditions.
Under the proposed loading, the HEA will develop a higher dislocation density than pure tungsten.
The HEA will exhibit smoother and more widespread dislocation flow with fewer pronounced pile-ups than pure tungsten.
The HEA will fail by ductile mechanisms, whereas pure tungsten will show brittle cleavage.
Pure tungsten exhibits high lattice friction relative to the HEA under the stated conditions.
Increasing temperature can facilitate thermally activated screw-dislocation migration between Peierls valleys in BCC HEAs.
High-temperature TEM artifacts and surface effects may complicate interpretation of the measured dislocation dynamics.
Thermally activated recovery and grain-boundary behavior could alternatively contribute to the observed deformation response.
A lack of significantly greater dislocation density and mobility, or similar fracture modes in both materials, would falsify the proposed lattice-distortion mechanism.
